import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_1.csv"
    
    # Define target output path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    
    # Load Source 0: userId, movieId, tag, timestamp
    df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    # Ensure correct dtypes for Source 0
    df_source0 = df_source0.astype({
        'userId': 'int64',
        'movieId': 'int64',
        'tag': 'string',
        'timestamp': 'int64'
    })
    
    # Load Source 1: movieId, title, genres
    df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)
    # Ensure correct dtypes for Source 1
    df_source1 = df_source1.astype({
        'movieId': 'int64',
        'title': 'string',
        'genres': 'string'
    })
    
    # Join Source 0 and Source 1 on movieId to get all columns for target
    # This is an inner join because we want only movieIds present in both sources
    df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on='movieId', how='inner')
    
    # Reorder columns to match target schema:
    # ['movieId': integer, 'title': string, 'genres': string, 'userId': integer, 'tag': string, 'timestamp': integer]
    df_target = df_merged[['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']]
    
    # Enforce dtypes again to be sure
    df_target = df_target.astype({
        'movieId': 'int64',
        'title': 'string',
        'genres': 'string',
        'userId': 'int64',
        'tag': 'string',
        'timestamp': 'int64'
    })
    
    # Save to target CSV without index
    df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
    
    print(f"Transformation complete. Output saved to: {target_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
